subject: Post-demo: OptiMed integration & model routing constraints
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@optimed.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@optimed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: OptiMed integration & model routing constraints

Hi Tom / Sara,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can line up a technical deep-dive with your infra team. High-level notes below, then action items.

1) Integration surface (SDK + auth)
- SDK: We recommend starting with our Node/Go SDK for the ingestion path (low-latency calls for triage and structured tool-calls). We can provide a sandbox token and a minimal example to wire up the streams.
- Auth: OptiMed prefers OIDC + customer-managed keys. We support OIDC and API keys; for Private/Dedicated deployments we can plug into your IdP via OIDC and rotate keys via KMS.

2) Routing & policy (latency / cost)
- Primary routing: route interactive queries to a low-latency Llama-2-Chat-70B-quantized variant in us-west for user-facing triage.
- Cost fallback: for batched/async tasks or overflow we suggest a fallback chain to a cheaper quantized Mistral-7B variant. Policy engine can set latency SLO = 250ms p95 and fall back on throughput thresholds.
- Region routing: sensitive PHI flows should stay in your VPC / dedicated pool (we can pin those to us-west-2).

3) Structured output & tool-calling (clinical protocols)
- Use our structured output schema for the triage form so the app can reliably parse actions (extractors + tool-call hooks).
- We'll demo how function/tool calling maps to your scheduling API and EHR links in the deep-dive.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Recommendation: host patient-embedding index in a private cluster; reranker model lives in the same region to avoid cross-region latency. We support on-the-fly rerank with hybrid ANN links.

Next steps / requests
- Action: Schedule a 90-minute technical deep-dive with OptiMed infra + security (please propose slots).
- Please attach or send the relevant security questionnaire (SOC2 / data flow diagrams).
- We'll share a sandbox token and the sample SDK snippet + network diagram (attached).

Attachments: optimed-mvp-architecture.pdf (network + model routing diagram), sla-draft-v1.docx

Thanks — I copied Monica (solutions engineer) who will run the deep-dive.

Best,
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ethan@redwood.com

- What does the fallback chain look like for a live chat session? If the cheap model returns less accurate triage, can we automatically escalate to the high-cost model and create a transparent trace for auditing?

We can do Fri 10–11am PT for the deep-dive. I will include our infra lead Sara.

Tom

From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@optimed.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@optimed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: OptiMed integration & model routing constraints

Tom — great questions. Short answers and supporting details below; we'll deep-dive on Friday.

- PHI and Private deployment: yes — for full PHI compliance we recommend Redwood Private (customer VPC + private control plane). That lets you pin all requests to your dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 and keep KV/embedding indexes in your network. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key rotation.

- Live chat fallback chain: policy engine supports multi-step fallback with tracing. Example flow: primary model (low-latency quantized 70B) -> if latency SLO violated or token cost threshold exceeded (configurable), route to the cheaper 7B variant; if model confidence/regression is below threshold, automatically escalate to 70B FULL or route to human queue. All routing decisions emit traces and are persisted for audit. We can export per-request routing metadata to your logging endpoint for downstream audit and QA.

- Embeddings encryption: yes — embeddings at rest can be encrypted with your KMS; we support envelope encryption. We also recommend hosting the ANN index within your dedicated subnet to avoid cross-cloud egress.

Attachments: sending the two files now. Also including a short SDK snippet in the Drive link for quick onboarding.

Proposed time: Fri 01 Oct 2027 10:00–11:30 PT — does that work?

Action items (from Redwood):
- Monica: prepare deep-dive deck that covers Private deployment topology, KMS integration, and routing policy examples.
- Ben: prepare cost analysis for the primary vs fallback chain at 10k qps (ballpark).
- Ethan: share sandbox token and quickstart SDK.

Thanks — looking forward.

Ethan
